simple.meaning: אָזַן (ʼâzan) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to weigh , i.e. (figuratively) ponder.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Ecclesiastes, beginning at Ecclesiastes 12:9. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָזַן (H239) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָזַן (ʼâzan) / H239 is traced through Ecclesiastes 12:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H239. azan II. [ אָזַן ] verb only Pi`el Perfect weigh, test, prove (compare Arabic weigh , also Arabic & Aramaic derivatives); וְּאִזֵּן (conj.) Eccl 12:9 (|| תִּקֵּן חִקֵּר, ). אזן (√ of following; Biblical Hebrew מאֹזְנַיִם אזן, ).
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root (rather identical with 238 through the idea of scales as if two ears);

occurrences.englishText: Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
